A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DMVR and alpha-DPG research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–H are readable and support comparison, including identifying removed experiments and relocated material.

before.justification: V1 reports original Lean theorem-proving experiments, diversity and difficulty analyses, and additional MATH/Minerva and Kimina-Prover experiments in Appendix G.

after.justification: V2 reports original Lean results, an expanded alpha sweep, and an online-versus-precomputed partition-function ablation in Appendix E.1.

M1.justification: The main Lean training procedure switches from a fixed partition estimate using 128 base-model samples to online estimation using four sampled responses. The target distribution, alpha-divergence objective, clipping, and leave-one-out baseline remain unchanged. Online estimation already appeared in v1's MATH experiment, so this is a localized procedural adaptation.

E1.justification: V2 removes v1 Appendix G.1's MATH Level-5 training and Minerva evaluation, and Appendix G.2's Kimina-Prover-Promptset experiments. Evaluation coverage contracts to the retained Lean Workbook setup, losing both informal mathematics and a separate formal-proving dataset.

E2.justification: The retained Lean comparison includes the same Base SFT, Dr. GRPO, High-KL, Rw-Ulkly, Pass@k training, ReMax, RLOO, and GPG comparators. Changes to highlighted curves and table membership do not introduce new comparators into this experiment.

E3.justification: V2 removes the Qwen-2.5-Math-1.5B, 1000-iteration study and the Kimina-1.7B, 8192-token study. Within retained Lean experiments, it expands the alpha sweep from six to thirteen settings and switches partition estimation from 128 offline samples to four online samples. The 7B model, 200-problem test set, 200 training iterations, and 1024-token limit remain.

E4.justification: Appendix E.1 adds a controlled test of whether more accurate, precomputed partition estimates improve performance. V2 also expands sensitivity and difficulty analyses near alpha = 1, while removing the explicitly shifted MATH-to-Minerva evaluation. The existing diversity, perplexity, and training-curve analyses are retained.

E5.justification: V1 Figure 12 reports per-model bootstrap uncertainty with n = 1000; v2 Figure 1 instead reports a frontier band representing one bootstrap standard deviation without stating the replicate count. Paired-bootstrap significance reporting at p < 0.05 remains in the corresponding Lean comparison tables.

E6.justification: The Lean results are replaced and expanded: alpha = 0.5 reports pass@1/pass@256 of 61.4/88.5% in v1 Table 4 versus 62.8/86.5% in v2 Table 3, and the best coverage moves to alpha = 0.25. V2 adds high-alpha and partition-ablation results and removes the MATH/Minerva and Kimina results. These are revised results under changed procedures, not controlled same-setting performance gains or losses.

T1.justification: Equation 6 adds the missing expectation over prompts to the forward-KL objective, making it consistent with the averaged gradient. The substantive proofs and derivations in Appendices B–D and H, including the support-decomposition theorem, remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and central DMVR, divergence-control, and Lean Pareto-frontier claims remain. The introduction and conclusion revise the best-coverage regime from intermediate to low alpha values, and the contribution statement drops its claim of an optimal trade-off.

C2.justification: V2 interprets the new ablation as showing no clear advantage from precomputation and motivates online estimation as avoiding additional sampling cost. Its limitations replace the bfloat16/long-sequence caution with an explicit restriction of the evidence to Lean and the DeepSeek-Prover base model. The central explanation of diversity loss remains.

D1.justification: V2 adds a code-repository link, explicitly documents FP16 training and evaluation temperature 1 with nucleus p = 0.99, and supplies hyperparameters for RLOO, GPG, and ReMax in Table 2. These disclosures do not independently establish changed settings. The earlier loss-normalization instruction is omitted, and the reproducibility statement still promises code release after publication.

R1.justification: V2 adds Holtzman et al.'s nucleus-sampling reference and removes Lewkowycz et al.'s Minerva reference with that experiment. Removing the duplicate Kimina reference does not remove that cited work. The broader positioning relative to RLVR and distribution matching remains unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 makes targeted revisions to training descriptions, results, contribution wording, and limitations; adds Appendix E.1; and simplifies Appendix G after deleting two experiment subsections. Affiliations and equal-contribution information also change. The overall narrative and section organization remain recognizable.

P2.justification: The empirical presentation is substantially revised: Figure 1 gains a redesigned frontier and uncertainty band, a partition-ablation figure is added, and the removed datasets lose their plots and table. Difficulty matrices and comparison tables expand and are rearranged. The training curves and theoretical illustration are retained under new numbering.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens the practical justification for online normalization and adds parameter coverage, reproducibility details, and clearer limitations. However, it removes two additional experimental settings and leaves inconsistencies: Figure 4 still plots alpha = 0.5 coverage near 88.5%, whereas updated Tables 3–4 report 86.5%. The methodological clarification, reduced validation breadth, and unresolved reporting consistency do not support a reliable net quality judgment.
